claims.claim_vi: Clearing is a process that calculates who should pay whom and how much; settlement is the process where real money moves between reserves in the settlement bank.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Pay-in flow: Bob buys a book on Amazon with PayPal; Amazon sends PayPal a money transfer request; because Bob's payment token is stored in PayPal, PayPal can transfer money on Bob's behalf to Amazon's account in Bank A.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Banks A and B send transaction statements to the clearing institution, which reduces what must be settled; if A owes B 100 and B owes A 500, the net position is that B pays A 400. The clearing institution sends the clearing and settlement information to the settlement bank, where both banks hold pre-deposited reserves, so the money moves between two reserve accounts.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Pay-out flow: Amazon tells the seller (Claire) she will be paid soon; Amazon issues a transfer request from its bank (A) to the seller's bank (C), where both banks record the transaction but no real money moves; both send statements to the clearing institution, which sends clearing and settlement information to the settlement bank, and money moves from A's reserve to C's reserve.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: There are three layers: transaction layer, payment and clearing layer, settlement layer; the first two are the information flow and the settlement layer is the fund flow; they are separated, and the actual money moves at the end of the day.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Because information flow and fund flow are asynchronous, reconciliation is very important for data consistency; and it gets more interesting when the buyer pays in one currency and the seller receives another.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: That clearing and settlement here describe one example (not every payment scheme) is the author's caution.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against payment-industry documentation.

design_notes_vi: Một lược đồ cho chặng Bob trả Amazon, hai khung bước cho hai lần bù trừ và quyết toán (cùng một dạng nên đặt cạnh nhau), rồi một khung ghi ba lớp. Sao kê, chênh lệch ròng và quỹ dự trữ được đưa vào thẻ chứ không vẽ thêm bên.
source_deviations: The source lists the pay-in and pay-out flows with numbered steps in the image; the lesson splits them by who acts and merges the clearing and settlement steps (1.4 to 1.6 and 2.3 to 2.5) into one card each.
The source ends by pointing at the buyer-pays-USD, seller-receives-INR case; the lesson links to the foreign exchange lesson instead of retelling it.
The "SDI book" example is replaced by "a book" to avoid an abbreviation that adds nothing here.
